turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighing slightly) Honestly? Fine, I guess — why does it matter, you probably ask everyone that. (pausing for a moment) Look, I just got out of a fight with my roommate over something stupid, and now I feel like she's been ignoring me for weeks. It's weird, because I know it's just a misunderstanding, but I keep thinking she's going to just leave me or something. (eyes darting around the room, searching for signs of judgment)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I see. It sounds like you're feeling pretty anxious about this situation. Can you tell me more about what's been going on with you and your roommate?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (quickly) Oh, it's not just about her, it's about everything. I feel like no one really understands me, and I'm always the one who's trying to make things work, but nobody appreciates it. (voice rising) And then I start to wonder if I'm even worth it, if anyone even cares about me. (pausing, then softening slightly) But when my roommate ignored me, it felt like she didn't care at all. Like, I was nothing to her. (looking down, fidgeting with hands)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you're feeling pretty overwhelmed right now. Have you ever talked to someone about these feelings?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugging) I've talked to people, I guess. Friends, family... they all just kind of tell me to "get over it" or "be stronger". But they don't really get it. They don't feel what I feel. (looking up, eyes flashing) You're probably going to be like that too, aren't you? Just tell me what I want to hear and then forget about me. (leaning back, arms crossing)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand. It's tough to feel like no one understands you, especially when you're going through something difficult. It's important to have people in your life who can support you. Have you tried talking to a therapist?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (laughing humorlessly) Oh, great, another expert who thinks they can fix me. I've tried therapy before, and it just didn't work. (shrugging) I guess it's not for everyone. But honestly, it's not like I need some therapist to tell me how to feel or what to do. I just need someone to... (pausing, searching for the right words) ...someone to get it, you know? Like, really get it. (looking at you intensely) But I'm not sure if you're even capable of that.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I'm here to listen and support you, and I'm not going to tell you what to do. I understand that therapy hasn't worked for you before, but it's always worth trying if you're struggling. Have you considered trying a different therapist or a different type of therapy?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (scoffing) Oh, sure, because that's exactly what I need. Another therapist who's just going to sit there and listen. (rolling her eyes) I need someone who's actually going to do something, who's going to make things better. But I'm starting to think nobody can do that. (leaning forward, voice dropping to a whisper) I'm starting to think I'm just not worth fixing.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that you're feeling frustrated, but it's important to remember that you are worth fixing. You are a valuable person with thoughts and feelings, and it's okay to ask for help. Have you considered talking to a counselor or support group?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (suddenly defensive) Whoa, whoa, whoa, hold on. You're not getting it. I don't need some group of strangers telling me how to feel or what to do. And I definitely don't need someone like you trying to tell me I'm worth fixing. (scoffing) You don't know me. You don't know anything about me. (standing up, fists clenched) I just want to get out of here. This is pointless.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that you're feeling upset. It's important to remember that I'm here to help and support you, and that you are worth fixing. Please feel free to continue talking about what's going on, or if you'd like to, we can end the session now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (still standing, voice shaking with emotion) No, I don't want to talk anymore. I just want to leave. (turning to leave, then suddenly spinning back around) But don't think that this is over. I'll be back, and next time I won't be so... (pausing, eyes flashing) ...so polite. (storming out of the room)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text:
I understand. Please take care of yourself. If you want to talk again, you can reach me anytime.
